In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neutrino oscillations are fully described in terms of matter-invariant quantities, which can be written as functions of matter-covariant quantities.
neutrino oscillation experiments in matter are sensitive to the neutrino mass hierarchy only in a very limited way and only for a few specific experimental conditions.
the exact matter-covariant form of neutrino oscillations is the most general and complete form for the oscillation probabilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neutrino oscillation probability is a function of matter- and phase-invariant quantities.

the matter-covariant oscillation probability is a function of matter-, phase- and trace-invariant combinations of neutrino oscillations parameters, and that the matter density can be expressed in terms of matter-invariant quantities and the vacuum neutrino oscillations probabilities.
we have shown that all neutrino oscillation observables can be written exactly in terms of matter- and phase-invariant quantities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutrino oscillation probability is invariant under the transformation of the matter density to a matter density plus a constant.
the probabilities for neutrinos and antineutrinos are identical if the neutrino mass ordering is normal.
the exact matter-covariant neutrino oscillation probability can be expressed in terms of only two matter-dependent functions.
